title: Dual Raster-Scanning Photoacoustic Small-Animal Imager for Vascular Visualization
protocol: Use a 532 nm pulse laser as the system laser source.
Set the repetition rate of the laser to 10 kHz.
Set the output energy of the laser to 100%.
Configure the trigger setting to external trigger using a user-defined program.
Couple the laser beam to single-mode fiber via an optical fiber coupler.
Collimate the laser beam using an optical fiber collimator on a two-dimensional motorized stage.
Deflect the laser beam using a two-axis galvanometer scanner.
Reflect the beam using a moveable mirror.
Focus the beam through a 4× objective lens.
Fix the self-made hollow ultrasonic transducer on the bottom of the objective lens using an XY translator mount.
Pass the focused beam through the center hole of the ultrasonic transducer.
Lock the Galva using a field-programmable gate array during water immersion microscopy.
Set the appropriate scanning range and speed by a user-defined program for WIM.
Lock the Motor using a field-programmable gate array during resin immersion microscopy.
Set the scanning frequency and number of scanning points using FPGA 2 for RIM.
Control the start and stop scanning using a user-defined program.
Use a 50-dB amplifier to amplify the PA signal.
Digitize the amplified signal using a data acquisition card.
Obtain the trigger signal through FPGA 1 or FPGA 2.
Process data and display images in parallel using a graphics processing unit.
Use a ring-shaped white LED with a color temperature of 6500 K, an illuminance of 40000 lux, and a diameter of 7.5 cm as the lighting source.
Remove lens M1, use a fixed mirror (M2) to reflect the light.
Record images using a CCD camera with 6.3 million pixels on the PA imaging system.
Display recorded images with display software.
Select a water tank measuring 10 cm × 10 cm × 4.4 cm, covering it entirely with a polyethylene membrane of thickness 10 μm.
Add sufficient ultrapure water to the water tank.
Place the prepared water tank on the working stage.
Turn on the laser switch and select the laser control program.
Preheat for 5 minutes.
Press the “ON” button on the pumping switch.
Set the laser parameters as per step 1.1.1.
Open the baffle of the laser.
Select the A-line collected program.
Press the “Start” button to capture a single point signal and display amplitude and spectrum of the current A-line signal.
Place a blade at the bottom of the water tank.
Immerse the bottom part of UT in the water tank for acoustic coupling, avoiding bubbles.
Adjust the position of Galva to avoid oscillation signals.
Ensure confocal alignment by adjusting the XY translator between UT and OL.
Adjust the height of the working stage to maximize the amplitude of the signal.
Determine the focus position.
Use a 5‒6 weeks old BALB/c mouse with a bodyweight of 20‒30 g.
Anesthetize the animal using urethane (1 g/kg) injected intraperitoneally before the experiment.
Conduct transition between WIM and RIM.
Use a planar ultrasonic transducer.
Shave the fur on the back of the mouse using a trimmer and depilatory cream.
Place the mouse on the holder (8 cm × 2.8 cm × 2 cm) in prone position.
Allow the imaging region to be in contact with the polyethylene membrane using ultrasound gel.
Avoid bubbles in the contact part.
Place the holder on the working stage for acoustic coupling.
Follow steps 2.3‒2.4 to start the laser and collect A-line signal.
Follow steps 2.6‒2.7 to align.
Press “Stop” to end the collection after alignment.
Select the WIM program.
Name the newly created folder.
Set the scanning parameter at 20 mm/s in the “Scanning Speed” tab, “20 mm*20 mm” in the “Scanning Area” tab, and “20” in the “Step” tab.
Click the Collect button to start scanning.
Click the Stop button to end scanning after acquisition.
Click Return to Zero to bring the Motor to zero.
Close the laser baffle.
Set the trigger setting to internal trigger.
Press the OFF button for pumping switch.
Replace WIM trigger as RIM trigger and connect it to the external laser trigger.
Press the ON button for pumping switch.
Set the trigger setting to the external trigger.
Click the Exit button to exit the WIM program.
Use step 2.4 to collect the A-line signal.
Open the laser baffle.
Follow steps 2.6‒2.7 to align.
Press Stop to end collection after alignment.
Select the RIM program.
Name the newly created folder.
Click the Collect button to start scanning.
Click the Stop button to end scanning after completing acquisition.
Click the Exit button to exit the RIM program.
Euthanize the animal using cervical dislocation at the conclusion of the imaging.
Use a focused ultrasonic transducer with central frequency 25 MHz and bandwidth more than 90%, focal length 8 mm.
Remove the hair of mice ear or scalp.
Make a small incision on the lateral side of the cranial temporal top of the mouse (depth to the skull) using a scalpel.
Start from this incision, use ophthalmic scissors to cut the scalp around the outer side of the skull.
Compress the bleeding point to stop bleeding.
Wash the wound with normal saline.
Place the mouse on the holder.
Allow the imaging region to be in contact with the polyethylene membrane using ultrasound gel.
Avoid bubbles in the contact region.
Place the holder on the work stage for acoustic coupling.
Use steps 2.3‒2.4 to open laser and collect A-line signal.
Use step 2.6‒2.7 to align.
Press Stop to end collection after alignment.
Select WIM program.
Name the newly created folder.
Set the scanning parameter to “10 mm/s” in the “Scanning Speed” tab.
Set the scanning area to “10 mm*10 mm” under the “Scanning Area” tab.
Set the step size to “10” in the “Step” tab.
Click the Collect button to start scanning.
Click the Stop button to end scanning after completing acquisition.
Click the Return to Zero to make the Motor return to zero.
Click the Exit button to exit the WIM program.
Euthanize the animal at the conclusion of the procedure while the animal is still under anesthesia.
Shave the hair of the mouse abdomen.
Place the mouse on the holder in supine position.
Allow the imaging region to be in contact with the polyethylene membrane using ultrasound gel.
Avoid bubbles in the contact region.
Perform steps 2.3‒2.4 to start the laser and collect A-line signal.
Perform step 2.6‒2.7 to align.
Press Stop to end collection after alignment.
Select the RIM program.
Name the newly created folder.
Click the Collect button to start scanning.
Click the Stop button to end scanning after completing acquisition.
Click the Exit button to exit the RIM program.
